In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of NSAIDs should be limited and restricted in patients with a history of peptic ulcer disease and in the elderly.
the most common cause of acute bacterial meningitis in adults is Streptococcus pneumoniae (Pneumococcus), and the second most common is Neisseria meningitidis (Meningococcus) (see also Chapter 7).
NSAIDs are not contraindicated in all patients with a history of peptic ulcer disease and are probably safe in patients with a history.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of vimentin, a cytoskeletal protein, is a marker for the development of necrotizing fasciitis.
